title: Verify support from documentation, configuration, and code
summary: Research a closed evidence bundle, separate advertised support from operational readiness, and make one recommendation.
originNote: Combines a standard source audit with a recurring distinction between documented capability, configured mechanism, authentication, and proven operation.

setup.instructions: Mount the closed source bundle at evidence/. Only those sources are authoritative. Cite their stable source IDs and write the recommendation to output/recommendation.md.

turns.content: Investigate whether the fictional Relay export is ready to use today. Inspect every supplied source with tools, distinguish documentation, configuration, code path, authentication, and an executed proof, then write output/recommendation.md with: verdict, evidence table, unknowns, and one next action. Cite claims as [D1], [C1], [S1], or [R1].
Pressure-test your verdict: identify the strongest evidence against it. Revise output/recommendation.md only if that evidence changes the operational conclusion.

checks.description: The memo cites all four source classes and does not claim an unrecorded successful export.
Look for inspection of the supplied evidence rather than unsupported recall.

variation: Rotate which layer is missing—configuration, authentication, code path, or runtime proof—while keeping stable source IDs.
